title: Brazil: Operacao Prato, the 1986 night and Varginha

lead.text: Brazil is the board's counter-example: its Air Force chased unidentified radar plots across four states on the night of 19 May 1986, its own Air Defence Command reported the phenomena as solid and showing a form of intelligence, and its UFO records now sit in the national archive.

summary.text: Operacao Prato was a Brazilian Air Force field operation run out of the Belem air base in Para, with the SNI, after mayors in the Colares area asked for help; a parliamentary document places it under the 1st Regional Air Command in Belem in 1977-1978.

On the night of 19 May 1986 the Air Force launched fighters from Santa Cruz and Anapolis against radar plots held by the CINDACTA network, over Sao Paulo, Rio de Janeiro, Minas Gerais and Goias; the Air Defence Command wrote the night up in a confidential report fourteen days later.

In Varginha, Minas Gerais, three young women reported seeing an unknown large-headed biped on 20 January 1996; thirty years later witnesses to the case briefed three members of the US Congress, and Rep. Eric Burlison wrote to the CIA and FBI for records.

From 2007 the Aeronautica, but not the Army or the Navy, began sending its UFO papers to the Arquivo Nacional in Brasilia, and a 2010 Air Force order requires originals to be sent on periodically, which is why the fund has no closing year.

record.text: The Air Defence Command's Relatorio de Ocorrencias is dated at Brasilia on 2 June 1986, addressed from the commander to the Comando Geral do Ar, and marked CONFIDENCIAL on every page; it was signed by Jose Pessoa Cavalcanti de Albuquerque as acting commander and is served by the Arquivo Nacional as BR_DFANBSB_ARX_0_0_0249.

The report's conclusion is that the phenomena were solid and reflected a form of intelligence, able to follow and keep their distance from observers and to fly in formation, and not necessarily crewed. It lists radar echoes on both the air defence system and the interceptors' own radars with visual comparison by the pilots, speeds from subsonic to supersonic as well as hovering, and altitudes from below FL-050 to above FL-400.

The report records the interceptor sequence with Zulu timings, 13 plots astern of the second Santa Cruz F-5, and pursuits abandoned at bingo fuel or on loss of contact; in the Anapolis area a pilot closed to two miles of a contact that zig-zagged, turned sharply and pulled away even while he was supersonic.

The report states its own limits: Brazilian coverage rested on radars built primarily for air traffic control rather than air defence, and the Command chose to confine itself to a simple narration of the facts so as not to give scope for speculation involving the Ministry.

The Senate's own open-data record gives RQS 193/2022, dated 16 March 2022 and signed by Senator Eduardo Girao and seven others, as a request for a commemorative special session. Its justification names the 1986 night, lists Operacao Prato among the Aeronautica's official UFO research programmes, and cites the 2021 US report released by ODNI.

The Arquivo Nacional describes the Fundo Objeto Voador Nao Identificado (BR DFANBSB ARX), held in Brasilia, as produced by the Comando da Aeronautica and composed of 743 registros; Portaria 551/GC3 of 9 August 2010 requires the Air Force's documentation centre to send originals to the archive periodically.

A 2011 Chamber of Deputies information requirement records that material was missing from the transfer: hundreds of photographs out of more than 500, with only about 230 supplied, several hours of super 8 and super 16 mm film, and the original, more detailed regional command reports. A Chamber document names the operation's commander as Colonel Uyrange Hollanda and records his death in 1997.

The national health register records the Hospital Regional do Sul de Minas in Varginha. On 8 July 2026 Burlison sent letters to the CIA and FBI asking for records on the January 1996 Varginha/Campinas incident.

Two foreign surveys leave Brazil out: the foreign-partner section of AARO's FY2025 annual report names only one London conference, and the Sky Canada Project report on national UAP reporting models does not use the word Brazil. Peru's state news agency, by contrast, measured the reopening of Peru's own office against Brazil and its neighbours.

claimed.text: BBC Brasil reports that at a press conference on 23 May 1986 the Minister of Aeronautics, Octavio Moreira Lima, with the five pilots and the controllers present, said five fighters had pursued 21 UFOs, that technically there was no explanation, and that a full dossier would follow within 30 days. The report was released only on 25 September 2009.

Pilot Armindo Viriato de Freitas said in a 1993 TV Globo interview that he knew of no aircraft able to match the speed of the object that pulled away from his Mirage. Civil crews also reported the lights that night, including the Xingu carrying Colonel Ozires Silva.

According to the same press account, a month after the night two officers of the Aerospace Technical Centre, with the American researcher James J. Hurtak, collected a press photographer's negatives for analysis by NASA, and they were never returned.

Jacques Vallee's diary, as quoted by another researcher, says that in 1988 Hollanda showed him the Prato military file, with photographs, aerial maps and trajectory analyses, at the regional air command in Belem, nine years before Hollanda's own public account in 1997. Vallee also reported claims that people were killed by the lights and injured in ways consistent with microwave radiation.

The American journalist Bob Pratt visited Colares from February 1979 and interviewed Hollanda, who told him his team took about three hundred photographs of eight different types of UFO; Pratt's file on the operation, which names Hollanda, his sergeants and the base commander who shut it down after four months, is served publicly by The Black Vault.

Book sources say the US AAWSAP programme built a Project Colares database of 346 records and that its contractor BAASS sent teams to Brazil in 2009; the Brazilian researchers they met say the teams collected from civilian ufologists and wanted artifacts. None of this rests on a DIA or BAASS document the board has obtained.

Neurosurgeon Italo Venturelli told members of Congress on 15 January 2026 that he examined a patient at the Varginha hospital and that it was obviously not a human being. Venturelli, Fortunato and de Sousa were brought to Washington by the filmmaker James Fox; de Sousa said a soldier threatened him, and an anonymous former soldier says he helped move the being to Campinas and heard that the Americans had it.

A Brazilian air traffic controller reported that a USAF cargo aircraft landed at Viracopos on or about 20 January 1996, and Claussen argued that such a flight would require US Air Mobility Command paperwork. Senator Girao attended the Washington events as a private citizen, not for the Senate, and promised Burlison to try to get evidence.
Press coverage in July 2026 reported that a US lawmaker, named as Burlison, had asked the FBI and CIA for records on the Varginha case.

contested.text: One account of Operacao Prato says it was closed after about four months having found no unusual phenomena, which sits against the injuries and deaths Vallee reported.

A 2010 Brazilian military inquiry concluded that the three women saw a local man known as Mudinho, crouched and dirty after heavy rain, and that the fire brigade, Army and sergeants' school vehicle movements were real events wrongly read as a capture and transport.

The records disagree about the Prato film. The 2011 parliamentary requirement says hundreds of photographs and hours of film were never transferred, but a federal court in 2023 upheld the dismissal of a suit to release them, holding that the claim rested mainly on press reports and witness accounts, and the archive told the litigant that a search on the operation's name returns six documents, none audiovisual.

The minister's public no-explanation stood ten days before a classified report inside his ministry called the objects solid and intelligent; but the report is addressed to the air command, and no document the board has obtained shows it reaching the minister himself.

The Air Force now says all its UFO material from 1952 to 2025 is in the Arquivo Nacional and that it has no specialists to investigate or give an opinion on the phenomena; the archive's own 2018 description ends in 2016, which the board treats as a stale description rather than a closing date.

AARO's 2024 report states that no investigation, including foreign efforts, concluded that any UAP report indicated an extraterrestrial origin, and the Varginha witnesses were briefing Congress against that finding.

On the board's reading, the hospital of the Varginha narrative is the registered Hospital Regional do Sul de Minas only by a reasoned match on name and city; no hospital record from January 1996 has been located, so the custody sequence there rests on testimony.

The board found no support for any claim that the 2009 BAASS teams met Hollanda, whose 1997 death rules it out. The Senate instrument that named the 1986 night was a request for a commemorative session, and the board records that any claim it compelled disclosure would be false.

questions: Was the 30-day dossier the minister promised ever written and withheld, or never written at all?
What do the six Operacao Prato items in the archive actually contain, and where are the photographs and films the 2011 parliamentary requirement says were never transferred?
The Air Force's finding for Prato was that nothing unusual was found, while Hollanda's 1997 interview and the Colares residents describe injuries and burns: what does the released file itself say?
When exactly did Hollanda die, and was any official inquest held?
Did the report of 2 June 1986 reach the minister, and did the Army and Navy ever hold UFO records of their own?
Is there any January 1996 hospital, transfer or flight record that bears on the Varginha custody sequence, and will the CIA or FBI answer Burlison's letters?
What did the 2022 Senate special session actually record and find?
